newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada oil firm to start Kenya operations in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Canada oil firm to start Kenya operations in Sept.

text.p: A little-known Canadian company that signed the first oil and gas exploration deal with Kenya in a decade said on Friday it would start seismic operations on the lands in September and start drilling in mid-1998.

Tornado Resources Ltd, which currently produces about 1,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in western Canada, said it committed on Thursday to an initial three-year exploration period in the Mandera and Lamu consessions in the little-explored east African nation.
The samll Calgary-based company, which expects to go public later this year, said it would spend a minimum of US$7 million shooting 275 km of seismic and drilling two exploration wells.

Tornado, led President Steve Mason, has an option for a second period with a minimum spending obligation of US$14 million drilling four wells. The deal also includes a third option to spend a further US$14 million, it said.
If Tornado excersised both options it would have a minimum capital spending obligation US$35 million over nine years, the company said.

The Mandera basin concession in northeast Kenya comprises 8.25 million acres and and Tornado said existing seismic indicated a similar geoligical structure of Ethiopia's 2 trillion cubic feet Calub condensate field.
The Lamu coastal concession near the Tanzania border has 3.5 million acres of land.

Brian Wilkinson, an owner of Toronado, said the company's straegy was to boost its operations in western Canada and hoped that success in east Africa would give it the ability to swap interests between the two regions with major oil companies.
Wilkinson said in a telephone interview that Toronado's executives had aimed to secure one or two deals before taking the company public.
"We wanted to get some major acquisitions and do it all at once. We didn't want the stock price jumping all over the place," he said.
The last time a company explored for oil in Kenya was in 1987 when Royal Dutch/Shell Group drilled some wells in the northwest Turkani region.
Tornado said a total of only 30 exploration wells have been drilled in the country and a number had indicated hydrocarbon shows.
